# A Fixed Ratio in Every Compound

## A Mixture Can Have Any Ratio

Stir sand into salt in any ratio you like: one spoon of each, or ten of one and one of the other. It is still only a mixture of sand and salt, and you decided how much of each went in.

<!-- STEP id="compounds" -->
## Water Always Has the Same Ratio

Water behaves very differently. Take water from the Ganga, from a borewell and from the sea, and purify each sample. If you break 9 g of any of them into its elements, you always get 1 g of hydrogen and 8 g of oxygen, a mass ratio of **1:8**.

Joseph Proust found the same kind of result for other compounds, and it is now called the **Law of Constant Proportions**, also known as the Law of Definite Proportions or Proust's Law. If you offer extra hydrogen to the oxygen, the extra hydrogen is simply left over.

<!-- STEP id="takeaway" -->
## Why Should It Be So Exact?

**In any compound, the elements are always combined in a fixed ratio by mass, whatever its source.**

Why should a substance be so exact, when you can mix sand and salt in any amounts? Two compounds of carbon and oxygen give a strong clue.
